name: high_temp_heat_pump_pcm_storage
title: High-temperature heat pump with PCM storage (Zorlu geothermal plant case study)
summary: High-temperature vapour-compression heat pump on cyclopentane studied for the Zorlu geothermal plant: geothermal brine evaporator with production pump, internal heat exchanger, water condenser delivering 7 MW at 141 °C to a phase-change-material storage; the evaporating and condensing pressures follow from pinch constraints evaluated zone by zone (superheat / two-phase / subcooling) in two PROCEDUREs, and a PCM sizing block gives the storage volume and discharge power.

authors: TBD (author of the original EES model of the Zorlu plant, not identified)
origin.course: no EES original is known: the example is not in CoolSolve misc/EES_ok.zip and the ULiège collection has no Zorlu/PCM exercise (searched 'zorlu', 'PCM', 'cyclopentane')

verification.reference: No independent reference exists (no EES original, searched CoolSolve misc/EES_ok.zip and ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models). Reproduction of the converged solution stored in ~/git/CoolSolve/examples/zorlu_heat_pump.initials, plus the cycle energy balance and pinch-point checks (see README)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py vs examples/zorlu_heat_pump.initials: "114 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 37" (the 37 extra variables are the state-point arrays P[i]/h[i]/T[i]/s[i], the balance check and the solved string variables added by the library model). With --rtol 1e-12 the largest relative deviation is 1.85e-10 on W_dot_sf_pp (round-off of the stored values). The shipped .initials (converged solution of the pinch formulation) is required: most solver configurations fail without it (CoolSolve examples/solver_robustness_report.md).

related_external: CoolSolve examples/zorlu_heat_pump.eescode (the example this model was imported from, kept in CoolSolve as a test case, with its zorlu_heat_pump.initials)
